description: Construction of 1 x 2 storey building and 1 x 1 storey building, including excavation of basement to create 2 x 1 bedroom single dwelling houses with associated soft and hard landscaping, refuse/recycle waste bin and bicycle storage. Installation of front boundary fence.

building_details.building_ref: Two-storey one bedroom flat to rear of site
One-storey one bedroom flat to front of site

constraints_details.result: Access Way To Back Of Shops Grove Green Road,
Right Of Way 316 To 332 Grove Green Road,

decision_conditions:
<ol start="1" type="1">
 </ol><p style="line-height: normal;"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;,serif;mso-fareast-font-family:
     &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:none;mso-fareast-language:
     EN-GB">The proposed introduction of two new dwellinghouses, by virtue of
     scale, intensity, layout and massing, would consitute over-development of
     the constrained site, creating uncharacteristic built form and plot
     layout, resulting in cramped and contrived form of back-land and infill
     development in the context of the area. The scheme is therefore considered
     to disturb the established urban pattern of the residential area.
     Furthermore, by virtue of its scale, massing and design, the proposed
     single storey dwelling would fail to preserve or enhance the character of
     the streetscape of Hampton Road by disrupting the established character of
     the terraced housing and reading as an incongruous and subservient
     addition to existing built form. In light of this, the proposed
     development would not be acceptable within the existing urban form in the
     vicinity and the wider locality in accordance with policies D1 and D4 of
     the London Plan (2021), policy 53 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan Part 1
     (2024).&nbsp;<o:p></o:p></span></p><ol start="1" type="1">
</ol>

<ol start="1" type="1">
 </ol><p style="line-height: normal;"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;,serif;mso-fareast-font-family:
     &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:none;mso-fareast-language:
     EN-GB">In the absence of the submission of a Tree Survey and
     Arboricultural Impact Assessment, to identify the impact of the
     development on the trees located within the vicinity of the development,
     along with the required protection and mitigation measures, a full
     assessment of the acceptability of the development and assurance of the
     protection of local biodiversity cannot be carried out, and therefore it
     cannot be confirmed that the development would be in compliance
     with&nbsp;Policies 79 and 80 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan and Policy
     G7 of the London Plan (2021).<o:p></o:p></span></p><ol start="1" type="1">
</ol>

<ol start="1" type="1">
 </ol><p style="line-height: normal;"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;,serif;mso-fareast-font-family:
     &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:none;mso-fareast-language:
     EN-GB">The proposed development fails to provide a&nbsp;soft landscaping
     scheme to visually enhance the site and improve biodiversity through
     appropriate green roof and ground level planting. In absence of sufficient
     urban greening, the development would result in significant areas of
     hardstanding and lead to poor quality of outlook, private amenity space
     and experience within the pedestrian access passageway&nbsp;for proposed
     occupants. Therefore, the proposal would fail to provide urban greening
     and biodiversity enhancement contrary to the NPPF (2023), Policy G6 of the
     London Plan (2021) and Policies 77 and 79 of the adopted Waltham Forest
     Local Plan LP1 (2024).<o:p></o:p></span></p><ol start="1" type="1">
</ol>
